candidate_commits.author: karthik14344
candidate_commits.subject: Faults: keep each fault live until the agent team is done; one-table campaign report
candidate_commits.body:
--wait-agents (run_fault, campaign) waits after the doctor's report until the
team's run finishes and saves agents.json, so the team works on the code that
is actually broken rather than on the revert. campaign --suffix keeps a new
campaign's runs apart. faults.campaign_report scores the doctor with the
evaluation's own scoring and adds the team's outcome per run.

The VM's .env takes per-VM overrides from instance metadata (aid-env-KEY), and
the agent team uses AGAI's own models unless AGAI_MODELS_FILE points elsewhere.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

candidate_commits.subject: GCP start-up: set HOME so models download; let Ollama's installer install the GPU driver
candidate_commits.body:
Without HOME, `ollama pull` failed silently on every first boot, so the VM
came up with no models. Installing a driver with ubuntu-drivers before Ollama
left two versions (595 + Ollama's cuda-drivers 620) and no working nvidia-smi;
now Ollama's installer alone installs the driver and the script reboots once.

candidate_commits.author: karthik14344
candidate_commits.subject: GCP start-up: Ubuntu's pre-built 595 driver before Ollama
candidate_commits.body:
NVIDIA's cuda-drivers 620 (what Ollama's installer falls back to) fails to
build against kernel 7.0-gcp. Ubuntu ships driver 595 pre-built for the gcp
kernel; installed first (with nvidia-smi), Ollama leaves it alone and runs
llama3.2 on the L4 at ~104 tokens/s.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

files.diff:
diff --git a/deploy/gcp/startup.sh b/deploy/gcp/startup.sh
index 2ae2873..909e931 100644
--- a/deploy/gcp/startup.sh
+++ b/deploy/gcp/startup.sh
@@ -41,10 +41,30 @@ https://download.docker.com/linux/ubuntu $(. /etc/os-release && echo "$VERSION_C
   apt-get update -q
   apt-get install -y -q docker-ce docker-ce-cli containerd.io docker-compose-plugin docker-buildx-plugin
 fi
+# GPU machines (g2-* carry an NVIDIA L4): Ubuntu's driver, pre-built for the gcp
+# kernel, BEFORE Ollama. With a working nvidia-smi, Ollama's installer leaves the
+# driver alone; its own fallback (NVIDIA's cuda-drivers 620, built with DKMS)
+# does not compile against kernel 7.0-gcp. Measured 2026-11-21: L4, driver 595,
+# llama3.2 at ~104 tokens/s.
+NVIDIA_PKGS="linux-modules-nvidia-595-server-open-gcp nvidia-headless-no-dkms-595-server-open nvidia-utils-595-server"
+if grep -qs 0x10de /sys/bus/pci/devices/*/vendor && ! nvidia-smi >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+  echo "=== installing the NVIDIA driver"
+  apt-get update -q
+  # shellcheck disable=SC2086
+  DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive apt-get install -y -q $NVIDIA_PKGS
+  if ! { modprobe nvidia && modprobe nvidia_uvm && nvidia-smi >/dev/null 2>&1; }; then
+    if [ ! -f "$ROOT/.gpu-reboot-done" ]; then
+      echo "=== rebooting once to load the NVIDIA driver"
+      touch "$ROOT/.gpu-reboot-done"
+      reboot
+      exit 0
+    fi
+    echo "=== WARNING: NVIDIA GPU present but the driver is not working - Ollama runs on the CPU"
+  fi
+fi
+command -v nvidia-smi >/dev/null && nvidia-smi --query-gpu=name,driver_version,memory.total --format=csv,noheader
 if ! command -v ollama >/dev/null; then
   echo "=== installing Ollama"
-  # On a GPU machine (g2-* carries an NVIDIA L4) Ollama's installer also installs
-  # NVIDIA's driver (cuda-drivers); it takes effect after the reboot below.
   curl -fsSL https://ollama.com/install.sh | sh
   # The patient containers reach it at host.docker.internal; the GCP firewall
   # does not open 11434, so it stays private to the VM.
@@ -53,18 +73,6 @@ if ! command -v ollama >/dev/null; then
   systemctl daemon-reload
   systemctl restart ollama
 fi

-    echo "=== rebooting once to load the NVIDIA driver"
-    touch "$ROOT/.gpu-reboot-done"

candidate_commits.author: karthik14344
candidate_commits.subject: GCP VM: keep the models loaded and warm them after every deploy
candidate_commits.body:
A cold model load (30-90 s) after boot, or after Ollama's default 5 idle
minutes, tripped HighLatencyP95 on a healthy app. Warm, the L4 serves chat at
p95 2.2 s and search at 0.09 s under the background traffic.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

files.diff:
diff --git a/deploy/gcp/startup.sh b/deploy/gcp/startup.sh
index 909e931..146d7f9 100644
--- a/deploy/gcp/startup.sh
+++ b/deploy/gcp/startup.sh
@@ -66,10 +66,19 @@ command -v nvidia-smi >/dev/null && nvidia-smi --query-gpu=name,driver_version,m
 if ! command -v ollama >/dev/null; then
   echo "=== installing Ollama"
   curl -fsSL https://ollama.com/install.sh | sh
-  # The patient containers reach it at host.docker.internal; the GCP firewall
-  # does not open 11434, so it stays private to the VM.
-  mkdir -p /etc/systemd/system/ollama.service.d
-  printf '[Service]\nEnvironment="OLLAMA_HOST=0.0.0.0"\n' > /etc/systemd/system/ollama.service.d/listen.conf
+fi
+# Ollama settings, re-applied every boot (Ollama restarts only when they change):
+#   OLLAMA_HOST=0.0.0.0   the patient containers reach it at host.docker.internal;
+#                         the GCP firewall does not open 11434, so it stays private
+#   OLLAMA_KEEP_ALIVE=-1  keep the models loaded. Unloaded after the default 5 idle
+#                         minutes, the next requests wait for a reload and the p95
+#                         latency alert fires on a healthy app (seen 2026-11-21).
+mkdir -p /etc/systemd/system/ollama.service.d
+want='[Service]
+Environment="OLLAMA_HOST=0.0.0.0"
+Environment="OLLAMA_KEEP_ALIVE=-1"'
+if [ "$want" != "$(cat /etc/systemd/system/ollama.service.d/listen.conf 2>/dev/null)" ]; then
+  printf '%s\n' "$want" > /etc/systemd/system/ollama.service.d/listen.conf
   systemctl daemon-reload
   systemctl restart ollama
 fi

--- a/deploy/gcp/vm-up.sh

+
+# Load both models now, not on the first user request: a cold load takes 30-90 s

+curl -fsS -m 300 http://127.0.0.1:11434/api/embed -d '{"model":"nomic-embed-text","input":"ok","keep_alive":-1}' >/dev/null || true

candidate_commits.author: karthik14344
candidate_commits.subject: Claude for the doctor and the agent team
candidate_commits.body:
Doctor: DOCTOR_PROVIDER=anthropic uses the official Anthropic SDK. Claude Opus
5.5 always thinks, so effort is set explicitly (DOCTOR_EFFORT, default high),
max_tokens has a floor that leaves room for the thinking, temperature is not
sent, refusals fall back server-side and then to DOCTOR_FALLBACK_PROVIDER.

Agent team: deploy/agai/models-claude.yaml selects AGAI's own Anthropic adapter
through CODEFIX_CONFIG - Opus 5.5 for manager/diagnoser/fixer (effort low/high/
high), Sonnet 5.5 as the judge AGAI requires to differ. AGAI code untouched.

The key travels as ANTHROPIC_API_KEY (secret aid-anthropic-api-key on the VM).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

--- a/.env.example

@@ -81,6 +81,9 @@ AGAI_MODELS_FILE=
 # requests on this repo) for the PR agent. Never commit them.
 ZAI_API_KEY=
 AGAI_GITHUB_TOKEN=
+# Claude: for DOCTOR_PROVIDER=anthropic (DOCTOR_MODEL=claude-opus-5-5) and for the agent team
+# with AGAI_MODELS_FILE=/repo/deploy/agai/models-claude.yaml. Never commit it.
+ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=
 AGAI_A2A_TOKEN=
 
 # ===== Deployment ===========================================================

diff --git a/deploy/agai/models-claude.yaml b/deploy/agai/models-claude.yaml
new file mode 100644
index 0000000..41faa15
--- /dev/null
+++ b/deploy/agai/models-claude.yaml
@@ -0,0 +1,52 @@
+# Model file for the agent team (AGAI) on Claude, read through AGAI's own
+# CODEFIX_CONFIG setting when .env sets AGAI_MODELS_FILE=/repo/deploy/agai/models-claude.yaml
+# (on the GCP VM: instance metadata aid-env-AGAI_MODELS_FILE). AGAI's code is
+# untouched: provider "anthropic" selects its own AnthropicLLM (official SDK,
+# structured outputs, prompt caching). Key: ANTHROPIC_API_KEY.
+#
+# Claude Opus 5.5 always thinks; `effort` sets how much (its default is medium,
+# so every role sets it). `fallbacks: default` re-runs a refused request on a
+# fallback model inside the same call (server-side, routed by refusal category).
+#
+#   manager           routing between 2-3 legal moves             -> effort low
+#   diagnoser, fixer  ReAct over the repo / writing the patch      -> effort high
+#   judge             AGAI's benchmark LLM-as-judge (not used when fixing incidents);
+#                     AGAI requires it to differ from the diagnoser and fixer
+provider: anthropic
+
+roles:
+  manager:
+    model: claude-opus-5-5
+    effort: low
+    max_tokens: 8000
+    fallbacks: default
+  diagnoser:
+    model: claude-opus-5-5
+    effort: high
+    max_tokens: 16000
+    fallbacks: default
+  fixer:
+    model: claude-opus-5-5
+    effort: high
+    max_tokens: 16000
+    fallbacks: default
+  judge:
+    model: claude-sonnet-5-5
+    effort: medium
+    max_tokens: 8000
+
+# USD per 1M tokens (list prices).
+pricing:
+  claude-opus-5-5: {input: 4.00, output: 20.00, cache_read: 0.20, cache_write: 5.00}
+  claude-sonnet-5-5: {input: 2.00, output: 10.00, cache_read: 0.10, cache_write: 2.50}
+
+pipeline:
+  max_attempts: 3
+  react_max_iterations: 8
+  max_rediagnoses: 1
+  rediagnose_below_confidence: 0.35
+  test_timeout_s: 180
+  allow_test_edits: false
+  rag_k: 6
+  prompt_variant: react
+  persona: default
